findings.title: Repo-map signatures can exfiltrate literal secrets as supposedly privacy-safe structure
findings.what: signatureOf only removes bodies and, for variables, initializer text. Function default values remain before the body (for example `function f(key='secret')`), and type aliases deliberately retain the entire RHS, including literal types such as `type Token = 'secret'`. renderFile then places those signatures into the prompt-facing map. This contradicts the stated privacy boundary and can expose credentials or other source literals, including data originating under ~/.claude if such source is mapped.
findings.fix: Generate signatures structurally from safe AST fields or redact all string/template/numeric/regex literal nodes before serialization; apply the policy to parameters, type aliases, enums, and other declaration heads. Add regression cases for literal type aliases and default parameter values.
findings.acceptance: Given source containing `export type Token = 'sk-secret'` and `export function f(key='pw-secret') {}`, neither generated RepoMap JSON nor rendered text contains `sk-secret` or `pw-secret`, while symbol names and non-literal type structure remain usable.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed type aliases call signatureOf with cutAtEquals=false, functions also retain pre-body text, the test explicitly expects a full type RHS, and generate.ts renders every exported signature verbatim.

findings.title: Repo-map rendering performs quadratic cumulative string joins
findings.what: Each loop iteration reconstructs the complete prior output with blocks.join before checking the budget, then joins it again at return. With a high caller-supplied tokenBudget and up to 4,000 files, cumulative copied text grows quadratically and can materially increase generation latency and transient allocation.
findings.fix: Track cumulative character or token-estimate length incrementally, check `currentLength + separatorLength + block.length`, append once, and join blocks only at return.
findings.acceptance: A benchmark or probe rendering 4,000 fixed-size blocks shows near-linear scaling and performs no cumulative join inside the loop; existing truncation semantics, including first-block inclusion, remain unchanged.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read lines 175-188 and confirmed blocks.join executes once per candidate block and again on return; maxFiles permits 4,000 and tokenBudget has no upper bound.

findings.title: Report-card recommendations lack structured artifact/field provenance
findings.what: The module emits action recommendations (KEEP, FLAG, MOVE) from attribution and reliability calculations. It exposes aggregate metrics and contributing session IDs, but does not record which source artifact and fields supplied each decisive claim or score component. Consumers therefore cannot reproduce a verdict from structured provenance alone, especially when telemetry, debug, registry, and transcript-recovered context are blended.
findings.fix: Attach structured evidence records to each project/verdict, identifying source artifact, session ID, field, observed value, threshold, and score contribution for every decisive attribution and reliability signal.
findings.acceptance: For each KEEP/FLAG/MOVE result, a test can reconstruct the drag score, bucket, attribution decision, and final verdict solely from emitted provenance records and verify each record points to an input artifact row and field.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the returned object includes aggregate counts, metrics, verdictReason, and generic contributingSessions only; no artifact/field provenance structure is defined or populated.

findings.title: Review-queue claims are not reproducible from emitted provenance
findings.where: src/lib/review-queue.ts:26-44, src/lib/review-queue.ts:104-133, src/lib/review-queue.ts:217-251, src/lib/review-queue.ts:269-293, src/lib/review-queue.ts:306-342, src/lib/review-queue.test.ts:115-238
findings.what: Each queue item recommends a session for review and states claims such as estimated spend share, retry storms, dead wall-clock, or likely unsuccessful outcome. Signals retain only prose plus a broad evidenceView; they omit artifact identity, source record/field, observed operands, and thresholds. The tests validate prose and view routing but cannot reproduce the claims from emitted structured evidence.
findings.fix: Extend ReviewQueueSignal with structured provenance entries containing artifact kind, session/record key, field, observed value, threshold or formula, and any derived operands; populate them in every add*Signals path and assert them in tests.
findings.acceptance: Every emitted signal has non-empty structured provenance, and tests reproduce its reason-driving metric and score from those records for cost, tool/API errors, debug, telemetry, context, and outcome signals.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass confirmed ReviewQueueSignal defines only category, severity, score, reason, and evidenceView; all signal producers and the full test suite omit artifact/field provenance.
